title: CRASH-057: tmp value reused after freed in string offset assign (use-after-free)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-use-after-free at Zend/zend_alloc.c:403 in _estrndup when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 8365e71cb92b, which postdates the release, and names the defect at Zend/zend_execute.c:535
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build crashes on it natively, so a silence on an arm is not a MISSED: under the judge's default scoring the case reads out-of-denominator on every arm; the sensitivity scoring (run-realphp.py --score-oracle-crashes) reads it by fault site instead.
fault_sites_why: ASan's access stack in our native run (results-ours-asan-default.json, sha256 045e3366bfc5) has _estrndup at Zend/zend_alloc.c:403 as its first frame inside PHP's tree (frame #1, under the libc leaf memcpy at frame #0, which is not declared: a fault there can be tied to this case only through its caller, and the launcher reports no return address); the stack's remaining frames are the interpreter's dispatch and are not sites On this platform the access is not the copy: the assignment keeps the temporary's buffer as the result's (the trigger's own account: the freed IS_TMP_VAR is reused as the assignment's result value), and var_dump($x) prints it -- php_var_dump, ext/standard/var.c:126, the PHPWRITE of Z_STRVAL -- through main/output.c and the CLI's write, which pass the buffer through. php_var_dump is therefore a declared site: the print of the reused temporary that the trigger documents, read off the source, with the nested arm's frame chain (residues/057-chain, 2026-10-28) as the confirming reading, not the admitting one.

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the nested layer present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: the corpus's pristine record for this case is 'SIGNAL:11': native PHP dies on a signal, so there is no pair to read

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same image with the nested allocator layer retiring the payload at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-deriving it under a fresh node when the cache hands the block to its next tenant: a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (php-real-object)
virtual-nested-pools.verdict_note: the corpus's pristine record for this case is 'SIGNAL:11': native PHP dies on a signal, so there is no pair to read

virtual-nested-exact.oracle: virtual-nested-pools with each payload bounded to the caller's request instead of REAL_SIZE(n): the arm that can see a defect inside PHP's own rounding slack (php-real-exact)
virtual-nested-exact.verdict_note: the corpus's pristine record for this case is 'SIGNAL:11': native PHP dies on a signal, so there is no pair to read

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the same trigger on stock CheriBSD purecap -- no nested layer at all, the real interpreter cross-built by ports/php/cheribsd/build.sh -- in the boot at the platform default (security.cheri.runtime_revocation_default=1, every_free=0): a SIGPROT at the ASan site with the bounds-malloc control faulting in the same boot, the same binary run with revocation off as the pair that attributes the fault, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json cheribsd-default)
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: neither a capability fault nor a clean exit -- ALLOCATOR-ABORT: CheriBSD's allocator aborted, the signature its own double-free check produces (ports/php/cheribsd/results/20261029-allocator-probe). Not a capability fault; with revocation off this case exited 0; NOT-REISSUED: no capability fault at the platform default, but the eager configuration (runtime_revocation_every_free_default=1) faults on this case, so the stale pointer IS followed. The eager fault lands after the script body, in request shutdown, which is what tells a revoked object apart from the allocator's cache being drained back to libc at shutdown. Context, not a verdict: every-free also faults on accesses nothing is meant to catch; out-of-denominator under the default scoring: the corpus's pristine record for this case is SIGNAL:11, so the unprotected program dies anyway and there is no pair to read. Run again with --score-oracle-crashes for the reading by fault site

status: built 2026-10-27 from the corpus and our native oracle; what has run is in this record's arms (verdict, verdict_from) and under results/
note: population: asan-blind -- ASan reports it only with PHP's allocator patched (cache off, no 8-byte rounding); with zend_alloc.c as shipped the run reads OK. That is the selection, by measurement; which mechanism hides it, and which arm sees it, is what the arms record. Collected by the corpus as history-5.x (historical-known, confidence high).
